questions.stem: What is 「書道」?
options: The art of writing characters with a brush and ink
The art of arranging flowers and branches in a vase
The art of preparing and serving powdered green tea
The art of folding paper into shapes
questions.explanation: 「書道」 combines 書 (write) and 道 (way): the way of writing. Flower arranging is 「生け花」 and the tea ceremony is 「さどう」; many traditional arts end in 道 because they are seen as a path of lifelong practice.

questions.stem: What is 「文楽」?
options: A classical masked drama performed on a bare wooden stage
Comic storytelling by one performer kneeling on a cushion
A theatre in which male actors wear bold stage make-up
A theatre of large puppets, with a chanter and shamisen
questions.explanation: In 文楽 each main puppet is worked by up to three puppeteers, while a chanter, the 「たゆう」, voices the story to shamisen music. Masked drama is 「のう」, and bold make-up on male actors belongs to 「かぶき」.

questions.stem: What is 「らくご」?
options: Comic storytelling by one performer kneeling on a cushion
A dance performed in a big circle during summer festivals
Classical poetry recited to the sound of a drum
A puppet play performed for young children
questions.explanation: A らくご performer kneels alone on stage and plays every character, using only a folding fan and a small cloth as props. The circle dance at summer festivals is 「ぼんおどり」.

questions.stem: Which statement about 「かぶき」 as it is performed today is accurate?
options: The characters are large puppets worked by puppeteers
Performances are given only once a year, at New Year
All roles, including women's roles, are played by male actors
All of the actors wear carved wooden masks throughout the play
questions.explanation: In today's かぶき every role is played by men; actors who specialise in female roles are called 「おんながた」. Carved masks belong to 「のう」 and large puppets to 「文楽」.

questions.stem: In the tea ceremony, what does 「いちごいちえ」 express?
options: A host should never serve tea to the same guest more than once
Every guest must bring a small gift for the host
Tea should only be served at the start of a new year
Treasure each meeting, as it can never be repeated exactly
questions.explanation: 「いちごいちえ」 (one time, one meeting) is linked with the tea ceremony: host and guests treat the gathering as unrepeatable and give it their full attention. It is now used for any encounter worth cherishing.

questions.stem: What is 「わびさび」?
options: An appreciation of beauty in simplicity, imperfection and age
An appreciation of beauty in bright colours and gold decoration
The strict order in which guests enter a tea room
The skill of balancing three branches in a flower arrangement
questions.explanation: わびさび values the quiet, the plain and the worn, such as a rough handmade tea bowl or moss on an old stone. It is an aesthetic idea rather than a rule, and it shaped the tea ceremony, gardens and pottery.

questions.stem: In a 「はいく」, what is a 「きご」?
options: A word that suggests the season
The title given to the poem
The poet's signature at the end
A word repeated in every line
questions.explanation: A traditional はいく includes a きご, a seasonal word such as cherry blossoms for spring or snow for winter. It places the poem at a moment in the year in very few sounds.

questions.stem: What is the traditional pattern of a 「はいく」?
options: Any number of lines with no set pattern
Three parts of five, seven and five sounds
Five parts of five, seven, five, seven and seven sounds
Fourteen lines that follow a fixed rhyme scheme
questions.explanation: A はいく has seventeen sounds in a 5-7-5 pattern. The longer 5-7-5-7-7 form is the 「たんか」, which is older than the はいく.

questions.stem: Who was 「まつおばしょう」?
options: A court lady who wrote The Tale of Genji
A manga artist who created Astro Boy
A poet of the Edo period, famous for his はいく
A painter famous for The Great Wave off Kanagawa
questions.explanation: まつおばしょう (1644–1694) made はいく a serious art and wrote a famous journal of his journey into northern Japan. The Great Wave is by 「かつしかほくさい」.

questions.stem: Which work is 「かつしかほくさい」 best known for?
options: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
The Tale of Genji
My Neighbour Totoro
The Narrow Road to the Deep North
questions.explanation: ほくさい's print of a huge wave with Mount Fuji in the distance belongs to his series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. It is a woodblock print, or 「うきよえ」, from the Edo period.

questions.stem: What are 「うきよえ」?
options: Ink paintings of mountains, made by monks living in Zen temples
Folding screens covered in gold leaf for castle halls
Hanging scrolls of calligraphy displayed in a tea room
Edo-period woodblock prints of actors, city life and landscapes
questions.explanation: うきよえ were printed from carved wooden blocks, so many copies could be sold cheaply to townspeople. Their subjects were city pleasures, かぶき actors and, later, landscapes such as ほくさい's views of Mount Fuji.

questions.stem: What is 「むらさきしきぶ」 known for?
options: Writing はいく on a journey into northern Japan
Writing The Tale of Genji at the Heian court
Painting The Great Wave in the Edo period
Founding the first school of flower arranging
questions.explanation: むらさきしきぶ was a lady at the Heian court in the early eleventh century, and her 「げんじものがたり」 is often called one of the world's first novels. The journey into northern Japan was made by まつおばしょう.

questions.stem: Who was 「てづかおさむ」?
options: A poet who wrote about a frog jumping into a pond
A manga artist and animator who created Astro Boy
The director of the animated film Spirited Away
A woodblock print artist of the Edo period
questions.explanation: てづかおさむ created Astro Boy (「てつわんアトム」) and many other works, and he is often called the god of manga. Spirited Away was directed by 「みやざきはやお」.

questions.stem: Which film directed by 「みやざきはやお」 won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature at the 2003 ceremony?
options: My Neighbour Totoro
Princess Mononoke
Kiki's Delivery Service
Spirited Away
questions.explanation: Spirited Away (「せんとちひろのかみかくし」) won the award at the 2003 ceremony. My Neighbour Totoro, Princess Mononoke and Kiki's Delivery Service are also his films from Studio Ghibli, but none of them won that award.

questions.stem: What is 「ゆかわひでき」 remembered for?
options: Founding one of Japan's best-known car companies
Winning Japan's first ever Olympic gold medal
Becoming the first Japanese person to receive a Nobel Prize
Becoming the first Japanese astronaut to travel into space
questions.explanation: ゆかわひでき, a physicist, received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1949 for predicting the meson, a particle linked to the force that holds the atomic nucleus together. He is often chosen as a significant person in the sciences.

questions.stem: At 「七夕」, what do people traditionally do?
options: Throw roasted beans to drive bad luck out of the house
Fly carp-shaped streamers for the children of the family
Display a set of dolls on tiered shelves covered in red
Write wishes on strips of paper and hang them on bamboo
questions.explanation: 七夕 recalls the legend of two lovers, represented by stars, who may meet once a year; wishes on paper strips called 「たんざく」 are hung on bamboo. Throwing beans belongs to 「せつぶん」, carp streamers to こどもの日 and dolls to 「ひなまつり」.

questions.stem: What is 「おぼん」?
options: A summer period for honouring the spirits of one's ancestors
The first visit of the new year to a shrine or a temple
A spring outing with friends to view the cherry blossoms
A winter festival of huge snow and ice sculptures
questions.explanation: During おぼん many families return to their home towns, visit graves and welcome the spirits of their ancestors, and communities hold 「ぼんおどり」 dances. The first shrine visit of the year is 「はつもうで」.

questions.stem: What is 「はつもうで」?
options: The last big clean of the house before New Year
The first sunrise of the year, watched from a mountain
The first visit of the year to a shrine or temple
The first meal eaten on the morning of New Year's Day
questions.explanation: 「はつ」 means first, and はつもうで is the New Year visit to pray for health and good fortune. The big end-of-year clean is 「おおそうじ」 and the first sunrise is 「はつひので」.

questions.stem: What is 「おせちりょうり」?
options: The rice and side dishes packed in a school lunch box
Special dishes eaten at New Year, many with a symbolic meaning
A boxed lunch sold at railway stations around the country
A bowl of noodles eaten on the last night of the year
questions.explanation: おせち dishes are packed in tiered boxes, and many carry a wish, such as black beans for good health and hard work. Noodles on New Year's Eve are 「としこしそば」, a different custom.

questions.stem: What is 「ぼんおどり」?
options: A dance performed at a shrine by a single masked actor
A parade of portable shrines carried through the streets
A dance class taken by children during the New Year school break
A dance held during おぼん, often in a ring around a raised stage
questions.explanation: People of all ages dance ぼんおどり at summer festivals, moving in a ring around a stage called a 「やぐら」 to drums and songs. Carrying a portable shrine is 「みこし」, a different part of festival life.

questions.stem: What is the 「さっぽろ雪まつり」 known for?
options: Fireworks over the harbour
Decorated floats in summer
Huge sculptures of snow and ice
Floating paper lanterns on a river
questions.explanation: The festival is held each February in さっぽろ, 北海道, and visitors come to see snow and ice sculptures, some as big as buildings. Fireworks displays, 「花火大会」, are mostly held in summer.

questions.stem: In 2013, 「和食」 was added to which UNESCO list?
options: The Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity
The World Heritage List of natural sites
The Memory of the World Register
The Atlas of the World's Languages in Danger
questions.explanation: UNESCO added 和食, traditional Japanese food culture, to its intangible heritage list in 2013, recognising practices such as respect for seasonal ingredients and New Year food rather than a single dish. The World Heritage List is for places.

questions.stem: What does saying 「いただきます」 before a meal express?
options: Thanks for the food and for everyone who provided it
Thanks to the cook, said only after the meal has finished
A wish for good health, said when raising a glass
A request to leave the table before others finish
questions.explanation: いただきます comes from the humble verb for receiving, so it expresses gratitude for the food and those who produced and prepared it. Thanks after a meal is 「ごちそうさまでした」, and raising a glass is 「かんぱい」.

questions.stem: What is an 「えきべん」?
options: A boxed meal sold at railway stations, often with local food
A small noodle restaurant next to a railway station
A lunch box made at home for a child to take to school
A train ticket that includes a meal on a long journey
questions.explanation: えきべん combines 駅 and べんとう. Many feature a region's specialities, so choosing one is part of the pleasure of a train journey; a home-made lunch box is simply a べんとう.

questions.stem: What do the two parts of the word 「カラオケ」 mean?
options: Empty and orchestra: music without the singer
Song and evening: a whole night of singing together
Voice and machine: a device for recording
Bar and microphone: a place for singing
questions.explanation: カラ is から, empty, and オケ is short for オーケストラ, so カラオケ is an orchestra with the voice left out for the customer to fill. Karaoke began in Japan and spread around the world.

questions.stem: What does 「にっけいじん」 mean?
options: Japanese tourists who are travelling overseas
Foreign residents who have settled in Japan
Japanese employees posted overseas for a few years
People of Japanese descent who live outside Japan
questions.explanation: にっけいじん are emigrants from Japan and their descendants, who may be the third or fourth generation born in their country. Employees sent overseas for a few years are 「ちゅうざいいん」, who usually return to Japan.

questions.stem: Which country has the largest community of people of Japanese descent outside Japan?
options: Canada
Peru
Brazil
Australia
questions.explanation: Japanese migration to Brazil began in 1908, and the community there is the largest outside Japan. Peru and Canada also have long-established communities, and São Paulo has a well-known Japanese district, Liberdade.

questions.stem: In the late 1800s and early 1900s, many Japanese men worked in Broome, Western Australia. In which industry?
options: Gold mining in the desert
Wheat farming on large stations
Shearing sheep for the wool industry
Pearling, diving for pearl shell
questions.explanation: Japanese divers were central to Broome's pearling industry, and the town's Japanese cemetery holds the graves of many who died in the dangerous work. It is one of the oldest links between Japan and Australia.

questions.stem: What is a 「姉妹都市」 relationship?
options: A plan to join two neighbouring towns into one city
A formal friendship link between cities in two countries
A partnership between two schools for student exchange
An agreement between two cities to share a sports team
questions.explanation: 姉妹都市 (sister cities) exchange visits, students and cultural events, and many Australian and Japanese cities have such links. A link between two schools is a 「姉妹校」.

questions.stem: 「ハワイのにっけいじんの家では、今もお正月におもちを食べることが多いです。」 What does the sentence say?
options: Mochi is eaten in Hawaii at New Year only by visitors from Japan
Families in Japan send mochi to their relatives in Hawaii each year
Many Japanese-descended families in Hawaii still eat mochi at New Year
Japanese-descended families in Hawaii gave up eating mochi a long time ago
questions.explanation: 「今も」 (even now) shows the custom has continued, and 「〜ことが多い」 means it often happens. A custom kept alive far from Japan is a good example for comparing culture across places.

questions.stem: Which description best captures 「おもてなし」?
options: Wholehearted hospitality that anticipates a guest's needs
A formal set of rules for seating guests in order of rank
The custom of bringing a small gift when visiting a home
A fixed service charge added to a restaurant bill
questions.explanation: おもてなし is care for a guest given sincerely and often before it is asked for, such as a hot towel offered as you sit down. Bringing a gift when visiting is a separate custom, the 「手みやげ」.

questions.stem: When would a Japanese speaker say 「もったいない」?
options: When a meal has been especially tasty
When something useful is being wasted
When someone arrives late to a meeting
When someone has worked very hard
questions.explanation: もったいない expresses regret that something of value, such as food, time or a talent, is being wasted. It is often used to encourage reusing things and finishing a meal.

questions.stem: What does 「がんばる」 mean?
options: To take a rest after hard work
To be naturally good at something
To persevere and do one's best
To win against a strong rival
questions.explanation: がんばる is about effort and persistence rather than the result, so 「がんばって！」 encourages someone before an exam or a match. Being good at something is closer to 「上手」 or 「とくい」.

questions.stem: What does 「えんりょ」 describe?
options: Holding back out of consideration for others
Speaking up confidently in a group discussion
Refusing to help someone in need
Arriving early to show respect
questions.explanation: えんりょ is restraint: not taking the last piece, or declining an offer once before accepting it. 「えんりょしないでください」 invites a guest to relax and help themselves.

questions.stem: 「日本の家にとまったとき、おかわりをすすめられても、一回はえんりょしてことわった。」 What does the writer's behaviour show?
options: She held back out of politeness rather than accepting at once
She disliked the food and did not want any more of it
She did not understand what she was being offered
Her host had told her that asking for more was rude
questions.explanation: 「すすめられても」 (even when offered) and 「一回はえんりょして」 show she declined the first offer out of restraint, a common polite move. Nothing suggests she disliked the food or was confused.

questions.stem: What do 「ほんね」 and 「たてまえ」 refer to?
options: One's family name, and the given name that friends use
A formal letter, and the casual message that follows it
The host of a gathering, and the guests who attend it
One's true feelings, and the stance shown to fit social expectations
questions.explanation: ほんね is what a person really thinks; たてまえ is the position expressed in public to keep harmony. The distinction is less about dishonesty than about awareness of context and relationships.

questions.stem: What does 「くうきを読む」 mean?
options: To read the weather forecast before going outside
To read a book aloud to a quiet classroom
To check the news on a phone every morning
To sense the mood of a group without being told
questions.explanation: くうき, air, here means the atmosphere of a situation, so 「くうきを読む」 is to pick up what others feel or want without it being said. Someone who fails to do so may be called 「KY」, short for くうきが読めない.

questions.stem: What does 「おつかれさまです」 express when said to a colleague?
options: A request for help with a difficult task
A complaint about feeling very tired
Recognition of the other person's effort
An apology for arriving late to work
questions.explanation: Literally 'you must be tired', おつかれさまです acknowledges someone's work, whether passing in a corridor or leaving at the end of the day. It is a greeting of respect, not a comment on how tired anyone looks.

questions.stem: In an interview, you need to explain a term that has no direct English equivalent. Which opening is most suitable?
options: このことばは英語にちょくやくできませんが、かんたんに言うと…
このことばは英語でも、もちろんまったく同じいみです…
このことばはだれでも知っているので、ここではせつめいしません…
このことばについて、私は何も知らないんですが…
questions.explanation: 「ちょくやくできませんが」 tells the listener no one-word translation exists, and 「かんたんに言うと」 (to put it simply) leads into your explanation. Claiming the English means exactly the same misleads, and refusing to explain ends the exchange.

questions.stem: Which sentence presents a personal opinion rather than a fact?
options: 七夕には、ねがいごとを紙に書いて、ささにかざります。
お正月には、神社やお寺に行く人が多いです。
私は、書道が一番おもしろい日本のぶんかだと思います。
書道では、ふでとすみを使って字を書きます。
questions.explanation: 「私は…と思います」 marks a personal view, and 「一番おもしろい」 is a judgement others may not share. The other sentences describe practices that can be checked, a distinction a good interview answer makes clear.

questions.stem: 「むかしは生の魚を食べなかった国でも、今では多くの人がすしを食べるようになりました。」 What does 〜ようになりました express here?
options: A decision that someone has only just made
Something the speaker has only heard about
An effort someone is making to form a habit
A change in behaviour that has come about over time
questions.explanation: Plain form + ようになる describes a gradual change in what people do: where raw fish was once not eaten, many people now eat sushi. A decision would be 〜ことにしました, and a deliberate effort would be 〜ようにしています.

questions.stem: 「おぼんには、多くの人がふるさとに帰るので、こうそくどうろやしんかんせんがとてもこみます。」 What does the sentence explain?
options: Roads and bullet trains are crowded at おぼん because many people go home
Many people stay at home during おぼん because the roads are crowded
Bullet trains run less often during おぼん, so the roads are busy
People travel into the big cities at おぼん to see the festivals
questions.explanation: 「〜ので」 gives the cause: many people return to their home towns, so expressways and bullet trains are crowded. Explaining why a practice has visible effects is part of placing it in context.

questions.stem: In an interview about ikebana, a student says: 「生け花を習いはじめたころは、ルールが多くてめんどうだと思いました。でも、先生に『花のいのちをたいせつにしなさい』と言われてから、考え方がかわりました。」 What changed for the student?
options: She gave up ikebana because there were far too many rules
Her teacher changed the rules so that they were easier to follow
She found the rules simple to follow from her very first lesson
Her view of ikebana changed after her teacher's words
questions.explanation: 「めんどうだと思いました」 describes her first impression, and 「〜てから、考え方がかわりました」 marks a change after the teacher's words. The teacher asked her to cherish the flowers' life; nothing says the rules changed.
